evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Exactly three permission actions exist: allow proceeds without approval, ask pauses pending canonical user resolution options, and deny blocks execution, emits tool.denied, and returns an error."

canonical_text: "Permission rules evaluate in strict layer precedence for mode override, parent/run ceiling, session cache, Persona overrides, project, global, and defaults, while child runs inherit restrictive action ceilings and argument-pattern rules additively without widening."

canonical_text: "Scope specificity resolves lane before seam before package before project before global, carries role-scoped account policy overrides, and preserves execution_entity_id, account_id, permission_scope, and approval_carryover_scope for multi-lane account-aware permission carry-through."

items.impact: This is the normative authorization spine: a single tri-state result, deterministic layer ordering, and non-widening child/account carryover constrain every downstream dispatch decision.
items.statement: Permission resolution is explicitly tri-state and ordered, with scoped account-aware inheritance allowed to narrow but never widen inherited authority.
items.title: Deterministic tri-state precedence and carryover

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "UI and runtime distinguish requested from effective permissioned capability state for tools, MCP, browser trust, project overrides, Persona profiles, and child ceilings, and disclose the governing layer on the owning surface."

items.impact: Owning surfaces cannot present requested authority as executable authority, preventing a misleading permission UI when a higher layer clamps capability.
items.statement: Requested and effective capability states, including the governing layer, are distinct runtime and GUI facts.
items.title: Requested versus effective state disclosure

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Granular permission rules may be simple action strings or objects containing pattern-based sub-rules that match invocation context such as file path, bash command string, or URL."

canonical_text: "Wildcard matching defines star, question mark, optional trailing command portions, tool-family prefixes, definition-order last-match wins, path case sensitivity from resolved root semantics, and fail-closed behavior when stable roots cannot be determined."
canonical_text: "Home expansion applies only when ~ or $HOME appear at the start of a pattern; mid-pattern occurrences remain literal characters."

items.impact: Different builders can disagree on escaping, malformed patterns, URL normalization, command tokenization, and canonical path comparison, yielding authorization divergence at a security boundary.
items.statement: The matching vocabulary and precedence are stated, but the excerpt does not define a parser/normalization contract or falsifiable outcomes for malformed, escaped, encoded, or canonical-equivalent patterns across path, shell, and URL contexts.
items.title: Pattern matcher normalization remains underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Any tool invocation referencing a path outside active project working roots triggers the external_directory permission key with default ask, except paths on the external directory allowlist, whose entries support wildcard syntax."

canonical_text: "An always approval derives a suggested scope from invocation context for bash, edit/read/glob/grep, webfetch/websearch, and webextract/webresearch/webcrawl/webmap, presents scope-bound choices, and binds canonical approval to approval_scope_key plus blocked-episode identity."

items.impact: Outside-root access defaults to an explicit gate, while durable approval reuse is tied to canonical scope and episode identity rather than an incidental UI session.
items.statement: External paths are ask-gated unless allowlisted, and any suggested always approval must remain scope-bound and episode-bound.
items.title: External-path guard and scoped durable approval

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Web operation permission keys derive from normalized domains and query categories rather than raw user-entered URLs, with explicit webextract, webresearch, webcrawl, webmap, and broad web*:* authoring vocabulary."

canonical_text: "Default web-operation posture remains ask where network web tools are enabled, six web tools stay explicit, and extract/crawl/map fan-out is visible in permission cards and audit payloads rather than hidden behind generic webfetch."

canonical_text: "Approval cards render tool-specific summaries for websearch, webfetch/webextract, webresearch, and webcrawl/webmap using query preview, target host or URL, task summary, estimated source count, root URL, and page/depth caps."

items.impact: Users and audit consumers receive operation-specific identity, scope, and fan-out instead of an over-broad generic web label.
items.statement: Web permissions use normalized derived keys, retain six explicit operations, and expose operation-specific summaries and fan-out in both approval and audit surfaces.
items.title: Explicit normalized web-operation approvals

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Web Once, For Session, Always, and Deny approvals preserve host-scoped follow-ons, wildcard-only MVP search/research, durable rule creation, and reject-all-pending cascade behavior under approval_scope_key and blocked-episode identity."

canonical_text: "Browser capture requests for screenshot or pdf require session_granted approval, browser permission storage values remain canonical while UI/source aliases are lineage only, and auth_session follows normal capture/share/clipboard permission disclosure."

items.impact: Concurrent pending requests or a session revocation can race a cascade/follow-on and leave some operations approved, denied, or captured under stale authority without a specified terminal state or rollback rule.
items.statement: The approval vocabulary and identity are explicit, but atomicity, ordering, cancellation, revocation, timeout, and partial-failure behavior are not defined for reject-all-pending cascades, host-scoped follow-ons, or session-granted browser captures.
items.title: Approval cascade and session revocation races lack oracles

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Special guards are synthetic permission keys tied to behavioral conditions rather than specific tools and are evaluated in addition to tool-specific permissions."

canonical_text: "doom_loop triggers when the same tool is called with identical input three consecutive times, defaults to ask, pauses or denies in headless mode, and allows configurable threshold and action."

canonical_text: "external_directory triggers when a tool references a path outside project working roots, checks the external directory allowlist first, and otherwise applies the configured allow, ask, or deny action."

items.impact: Retries, reordered parallel calls, semantically identical serialized inputs, symlink changes, and root changes can produce inconsistent guard activation or allowlist bypass.
items.statement: Synthetic guards compose with tool permissions, but the excerpt does not define doom-loop comparison serialization, counter scope/reset under concurrency, or external-path canonicalization and time-of-check behavior.
items.title: Guard identity and canonicalization are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "external_publish_side_effect covers DockerHub repository creation, autonomous DockerHub image push, managed remote template repository creation, and managed Unraid template repository remote push as non-bypassable remote side-effect approvals."

canonical_text: "A direct user click approves only the exact remote side effect named by that control, chained remote side effects require separate approvals in execution order, and blocked or rejected runtime errors identify the blocked step, guard, and recovery actions inline and in chat/evidence output."

items.impact: Remote publication cannot inherit generic authority or a neighboring click, and users receive step-specific recovery information when a chain stops.
items.statement: External publication is a non-bypassable, exact-side-effect gate, with separate ordered approvals and visible failure/recovery details for chained actions.
items.title: Non-bypassable external publication chain

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Ask flow preset behavior carries TODO, plan-mode web, batch webfetch, four-tier approval ladder, web tool visibility, strict read_only/no-network options, blocked/unavailable payload fields, and skill/lsp/question/todo/web keys through permission presets."

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Permission resolution composes precedence layers with dispatch checks by building invocation context, applying mode and scoped layers, running non-bypassable guards and capability gates, persisting requested/effective evidence, rechecking hook mutations, and dispatching only final allow outcomes."

canonical_text: "Arg-touching hooks require permission checks on the original invocation and the modified invocation before dispatch, in the required order from context normalization through final dispatch."

items.impact: A mutable invocation or policy snapshot can change after the final check, and textual scanning can miss destructive behavior introduced through shell parsing, encoding, environment expansion, scripts, or indirection.
items.statement: The check order is explicit, but the excerpt lacks an atomic invocation/policy snapshot through dispatch and a shell-semantic oracle for destructive-command detection beyond scanning the full command string.

items.impact: Permissions can rely on isolation without duplicating or contradicting the lifecycle contract owned by execution components.
items.statement: The shell isolation dependency and its owning documents are explicitly identified; Permissions is a consumer, not a second lifecycle owner.
items.title: Shell isolation ownership boundary is explicit

items.impact: A stale cleanup eligibility read can delete a target that acquired a new owner/dependency, and competing writers can lose or corrupt durable permission rules without atomic compare-and-swap semantics.
items.statement: Cleanup blockers and storage layers are named, but the excerpt does not define atomic eligibility revalidation at deletion time or locking, transactional writes, conflict detection, and crash recovery for concurrent TOML mutations.

items.statement: Durable record identity and canonical TOML ownership are clear, but projection update ordering, versioning, restart reconciliation, and recovery from a write that succeeds in only one store are not specified.

segments.summary: Reviewed the tri-state action contract, layered and account-aware precedence, requested/effective disclosure, and path/shell/URL matcher semantics; found missing normalization and malformed-input oracles.

Reviewed external-directory approval, normalized web keys and summaries, session ladders, and browser capture boundaries; found unresolved cascade, revocation, timeout, and partial-failure transitions.
Reviewed synthetic guards, external publication approvals and recovery, and taxonomy/Ask ownership; found guard comparison, reset, and canonicalization behavior underspecified.
Reviewed preset and approval lifetimes, blocked recovery, audit visibility, tool-owner seams, batch bounds, and multi-lane HITL; found audit lifecycle and recovery-action freshness gaps.
Reviewed Plan/read-only/automation distinctions, composed dispatch, full-command checks, hook rechecks, and shell ownership; found dispatch TOCTOU and shell-semantic bypass risk.
Reviewed cleanup retention gates, durable layered TOML, metadata records, redb projection, and effective/debug disclosure; found cleanup/storage atomicity and projection recovery gaps.

Reviewed run-scoped debug grants, deterministic target binding, Permissions tab/editor structure, and preset matrices; found resume/expiry races and missing accessibility, localization, and deletion recovery.

Reviewed allowlist and doom-loop controls, Persona/scope/cross-surface mutations, ELI5/Expert copy, and threat boundaries; found sensitive-control recovery, mutation conflicts, and threat/oracle gaps.
